title: introduce-retry-mapper-and-generator-friendly-stream-facade
author: Rhea Patel
description:
Motivation: unify retry configuration semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and make streaming generators/pull-streams friendlier to ergonomic iteration. This PR adds a compact retry-mapper (profiles -> transport hints), generator-friendly stream facade (backpressure-safe async generator wrappers for TS/Py and safe channel iterator for Go), and a small credential catalog shim to reduce surface differences between SDKs.

What changed (single continuous description): Implemented retry-mapper that translates high-level retry profiles (fast, balanced, hedged) into concrete transport hints (backoff base, max_retries, hedging_window). Added generator-friendly facade that introduces a minimal adapter so existing generator/pullstream users have a single ergonomic API across languages. For Python: new async_generator helpers + RetryMapper and StreamAdapter classes in redwood_sdk/streaming; for TypeScript: added generator-friendly AsyncGeneratorWrapper and retry/profile mapping in src/stream and src/retry; for Go: introduced streamiter package with ChannelIterator and retrymap package for mapping profiles to RetryOptions. Added a lightweight credentials catalog (cred_catalog) used only at SDK surface to pick sensible defaults for token refresh windows and telemetry tags. Updated docs and examples, bumped minor versions (py 0.19.0 -> 0.20.0, ts 1.27.0 -> 1.28.0, go 1.8.0 -> 1.9.0). Contains migration notes and compatibility layer so existing call sites keep working.

Testing & perf: unit tests added across sdks, e2e coupling test exercising streaming reconnect+retry combinations was added to the monorepo harness. Local perf runs show <2% median-latency regressions for typical short-stream workloads and 18-24% per-token cost savings for batched generator flows (due to smarter retry/hedging defaults and warmed session hints).

Backwards compatibility: default retry profiles map to existing numeric defaults where possible; advanced users can still pass explicit RetryOptions. This change is intended to be non-breaking for most customers; SDK consumers that relied on undocumented retry knobs may see a difference in hedging behavior — release notes highlight this.

Follow-ups: annotate templates with additional telemetry fields (ENG-10040), expose retry-mapper config via console (product work item), and port the credential-catalog to Redwood Private installer for consistent defaulting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Cross-SDK type and shape parity for public APIs
- [x] Unit and integration tests updated
- [x] Docs and migration guide drafted
- [x] Version bumps for all three SDKs
- [x] CI green and canary run validated

Maya Srinivasan: Suggestion to ensure hedging defaults are opt-in for low-tier hosted customers to avoid cost surprises. Asked for a feature-flag fallback.
Rhea Patel (author): Added feature flag 'enable_hedging' default=false for free-tier clients and documented in migration guide. Confirmed tests cover both paths.
Julian Park: Requested more unit tests around generator cancellation edge cases.

release_notes: Added RetryMapper (profiles -> transport hints) and generator-friendly stream facades across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Introduced a lightweight credential catalog used for sensible token refresh defaults. Non-breaking for most users; hedging behavior has an opt-in feature flag for free-tier customers. SDK minor versions bumped: py 0.20.0, ts 1.28.0, go 1.9.0. See docs/sdk/migration/retry-mapper.md for migration steps.
notes_for_support: Support: be aware of SUP-4312 where a customer in free-tier reported unexpected hedging behavior after upgrading their app. We added a feature-flag default to mitigate; rollout notes in the ChangeLog and migration guide. If customers report increased cost after upgrade, confirm feature-flag status and advise pinning explicit RetryOptions.
